code_summary: ocmsadminui pages/PS/{form/PSForm,form/PSDetails,form/PSSummary,list/PSList,page/PS,page/PSView}.tsx, pages/NoticeSearch/hook/{ApplyOperationAction.tsx,useBatchOperation.ts}, context/OptionsContext.tsx, utils/{mapping,validation}/PS/PS.ts, utils/constant.ts. ocmsadminapi workflows/notice_creation/core/SuspensionProcessingController (staff-apply-suspension, staff-revive-suspension, staff-check-suspension-eligibility), core/helpers/{PermanentSuspensionHelper,SuspensionBaseHelper,SuspensionProcessingHelper,PermanentRevivalHelper,RevivalBaseHelper}, crud/ocmsizdb/suspendednotice/SuspendedNotice, api-authorization.properties (OCMS_APPLY_PS). ocmsadminprivateapi, ocmseserviceapi, ocmseserviceui, thirdpartyapi: not used by this staff PS flow
note: Status in stories.json is 'Fully paid'; there is no OCMS flow deck. The main path is in the UI: for notices that already have a PS (and are not paid), PSForm first calls staff-revive-suspension (reason PSR) and then staff-apply-suspension. Revival only fills date_of_revival, revival_reason, remarks, officer on the old suspended_notice rows (no delete), and the new PS row is added with a new sr_no. Three remarks: (1) revive and apply are two separate requests without rollback, so if apply fails on a per-code stage rule the old PS is already revived and the notice has no PS; (2) the server safety-net path (reviveOldPS) swallows exceptions and uses reason CSR, different from PSR on the UI path; (3) for paid notices (PS-FP/PRA) only codes CFA and VST can be chosen from the UI. Revival through this endpoint also revives active TS on the same notice. Maintenance tickets: OCMS-DF-2026-114 and OCMS-DF-2026-129 (Closed; an_flag is reset when PS-ANS is revived, PermanentRevivalHelper.java:206-240), OCMS-DF-2026-075 (Closed; re-applying PS on a paid notice, PermanentSuspensionHelper.java:82-95), OCMS-DF-2026-152 (Ready to DEV/In SIT, open; refundNoticeId from the PLUS path is wrong, not the staff UI path; the code at PermanentSuspensionHelper.java:358-366 already returns the refund id, whether the ticket is reflected on main cannot be verified from the repo).
recommendation: Partial claim: auto-revive without deleting old records and adding the new PS work in the normal case; the atomicity of revive+apply, the server safety net and the code limits for paid notices need fixing or acceptance by URA as limits

steps.step: OCMS detects notices that already have a permanent suspension and revives it automatically before the new code is applied, without extra officer action
steps.detail: In onAPI, notices with suspensionType PS and no crsReasonOfSuspension (not paid) are collected as noticesToRevive and POSTed to staff-revive-suspension with revivalReason PSR and revivalRemarks 'Permanent Suspension Revival' (PSForm.tsx:114-129, PS.ts:29-43). Notices whose revival succeeds are added to the apply list, failed ones are recorded as failed (PSForm.tsx:130-137). There is no extra click beyond the confirmation of story 18.8. The staff-revive-suspension endpoint is allowed for OCMS_APPLY_PS (api-authorization.properties:61-63).

steps.step: Revival records the closing of the old permanent suspension on the same row without deleting the old record
steps.detail: revivePS takes all active suspensions (date_of_revival NULL) and updateSuspendedNoticeRevival fills date_of_revival, revival_reason, revival_remarks, officer_authorising_revival through a native UPDATE; there is no delete in this path (RevivalBaseHelper.java:278-296, 719-724). If no active suspension remains, VON and eVON are cleared (RevivalBaseHelper.java:748-753). Because it targets all active suspensions, active TS on the same notice is revived too (PermanentRevivalHelper.java:177-178); that is a side effect the story does not mention. For PS-ANS, an_flag is reset to N (PermanentRevivalHelper.java:206-240, OCMS-DF-2026-114 and OCMS-DF-2026-129, Closed).

steps.step: OCMS applies the new permanent suspension code as a new record while the old record stays stored
steps.detail: After revival, staff-apply-suspension runs processPS: updateVON sets epr_reason_of_suspension to the new code and insertSuspendedNotice adds a new row with a new sr_no from the sequence (SuspensionBaseHelper.java:340-348, 443-467; SuspensionProcessingController.java:997). The old PS row is not touched again, so the history (old: revived, new: active) is kept in ocms_suspended_notice. There is no delete operation in PermanentSuspensionHelper or SuspensionBaseHelper (grep result).

steps.step: The server still revives the old PS before applying the new code if the notice is still PS (server-side safety net)
steps.detail: processPS calls reviveOldPS if the notice is still of type PS, used for paid notices (which the UI does not revive) or other API callers. The revival reason on this path is CSR ('Permanent Suspension Revival' or 'Change suspension reason' for paid notices), different from PSR on the UI path (PermanentSuspensionHelper.java:256-271), so two revival data patterns appear for the same action. If reviveOldPS throws, it is only logged and the new PS is still applied (PermanentSuspensionHelper.java:301-304), so two active PS can exist without any error to the officer. If the code equals the existing PS, the request is treated as idempotent and changes nothing (PermanentSuspensionHelper.java:78-97).

steps.step: Applies to any existing permanent suspension, including on notices that are already paid (PS-FP/PRA)
steps.detail: For paid notices with PS FP or PRA, the UI only continues if the form code is APP, CFA or VST; otherwise the notice goes to the failed list 'Not allowed to apply new PS code to paid Notice(s).' (PSForm.tsx:103-111). Because APP is not in APPLY_PS_ALLOWED (constant.ts:114-115), only CFA and VST can be used from the staff UI. The server rejects other codes with 'Paid/partially paid notices only allow APP, CAN, CFA, or VST' (PermanentSuspensionHelper.java:180-192, 212-220), revives the old PS with CSR and creates a refund record (PermanentSuspensionHelper.java:259-262, 321-377); creating the refund is not mentioned in this story. Related tickets: OCMS-DF-2026-075 (Closed) and OCMS-DF-2026-152 (open, PLUS path; whether it is reflected on main cannot be verified from the repo).

steps.step: Revival and applying the new code run as one unit so the notice does not lose its PS if applying fails
steps.detail: Revive (staff-revive-suspension) and apply (staff-apply-suspension) are two HTTP requests each with its own @Transactional (SuspensionProcessingController.java:214-215, 622-624); there is no rollback across them. The early eligibility when choosing notices only checks the common stage list (SuspensionProcessingHelper.java:283-295), while the per-code stage rules are only checked at apply (e.g. ANS only ENA/RD1, CAN only NPA/ROV/ENA/RD1; SuspensionBaseHelper.java:236-244, 274-276). Example: a notice at stage DN1 with PS-FOR replaced by ANS passes eligibility and revival, but apply fails. The result is that the old PS is already revived (VON cleared), the new PS does not go in, and the UI only shows that notice as failed without restoring the old PS (PSForm.tsx:149-160). This is a conclusion from reading the flow; not tested in an environment.
